title: Felix and the Gravity
premise: Mara Dravenmoor, a xenolinguist exiled to a forgotten beacon station after refusing to weaponize a language, has spent nine years translating nothing—until a distress signal arrives in Ashkari, a tongue officially extinct since the war's first atrocity. The signal is from the Ashkari survivors everyone believed dead, and it contains proof that the war's founding genocide was ordered, not accidental. Pursued by both fleets and shadowed by Ilex, a defector pilot who becomes their reluctant found family, Mara must choose between delivering the truth and protecting the only people who ever stayed. In the end, Mara broadcasts the message openly, sacrificing the beacon and nearly themself, forcing both sides to face the record—and finding belonging not in a home, but in the people who choose to stay.
about_author: Casper Villalobos is the pen name of a former radio technician who spent six years maintaining remote relay stations in the Andes before turning to fiction. They write about lonely outposts, impossible languages, and the quiet radicalism of staying.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Ordered
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Establishes daily life on Station Vesper-9: maintenance rituals, one-sided conversations with the beacon, dreams that arrive in no human tongue. A supply drone arrives with a note questioning why the station still exists. Emotional beat: comfortable loneliness curdling into doubt.

chapters.title: Signal in a Dead Mouth
chapters.summary: Mara intercepts a repeating distress transmission and recognizes Ashkari—a language she helped classify before its speakers were annihilated. She verifies it three times before believing it. Emotional beat: awe shading into dread, because speaking this language is itself a crime.

chapters.title: Ilex Falls Out of the Sky
chapters.summary: Ilex's POV. A damaged scout ship crash-lands near the station; its pilot claims to be a salvager but carries military encryption keys. Mara patches the hull; Ilex lies about everything else. Emotional beat: wary mutual usefulness, two people fluent in concealment.

chapters.title: Grammar of the Vanished
chapters.summary: Mara decodes the distress signal: coordinates, a census of survivors, and a fragment implicating Fleet Command in the Ashkari bombardment. Ilex watches her work and quietly recognizes what the data means. Emotional beat: the thrill of translation giving way to horror.

chapters.title: What the War Was For
chapters.summary: Ilex confesses they're a deserter who saw the strike orders and ran. Mara admits she was dismissed for refusing to build an Ashkari deception protocol. Two liars trade truths. Emotional beat: the fragile first stone of trust laid down.

chapters.title: Ping
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The beacon logs an unauthorized query from Fleet intelligence—the station's invisibility is failing. They have maybe weeks before someone comes. Emotional beat: paranoia tightening like a ratchet; the past arriving on schedule.

chapters.title: The Survivors' Chorus
chapters.summary: Mara answers the distress signal. The reply is not one voice but hundreds, layered recordings of the last living Ashkari speakers asking to be heard. She weeps at grammar she thought buried. Emotional beat: grief and responsibility entwined.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Heading
chapters.summary: Ilex's POV. Both warring factions detect the Ashkari transmission burst and redirect ships toward its origin. Ilex calculates interception times and realizes rescue and annihilation will arrive together. Emotional beat: cold arithmetic masking panic.

chapters.title: Everything I Left
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Mara's POV: her tribunal, her mentor's betrayal, the choice that made her unemployable. She understands now that exile was protection—for the fleet, not from it. Emotional beat: old wound reopened as context for the choice ahead.

chapters.title: The Deception Protocol
chapters.summary: Fleet offers Mara reinstatement if she decrypts the signal privately so Command can suppress it. The offer arrives with a threat against Ilex. Emotional beat: temptation wearing a familiar face; loyalty and truth pulling apart.

chapters.title: Small Hours, Small Kindnesses
chapters.summary: A quiet interlude: repairs, shared meals, Ilex teaching Mara a card game, Mara teaching Ilex Ashkari lullabies. Neither names what the station has become. Emotional beat: found family forming in the negative space of catastrophe.

chapters.title: Interception
chapters.summary: A Fleet corvette arrives early. Ilex flies a decoy run in the repaired scout ship while Mara hides the translation core in the beacon's own housing—invisible inside the thing nobody remembers. Emotional beat: terror, competence, and the first real sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Price of the Decoy
chapters.summary: Ilex's POV. The decoy works but the ship is crippled; Ilex limps back burned and half-frozen. Mara realizes she almost lost the only person who stayed without being ordered to. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into fierce, unspoken devotion.

chapters.title: Command's Voice
chapters.summary: Admiral Sefu Okafor hails the station directly: surrender the linguist and the data, or be listed as enemy infrastructure. He speaks to Mara like a colleague, which is worse. Emotional beat: institutional intimacy as menace.

chapters.title: What the Ashkari Ask
chapters.summary: The survivors send a final addendum: they don't want vengeance or asylum—they want the full record broadcast in both fleets' languages, in Ashkari, unedited, even if it dooms them. Mara must decide whether they get to make that demand of her. Emotional beat: agency returned to the silenced.

chapters.title: Loyalty Is a Direction, Not a Flag
chapters.summary: Mara and Ilex argue: deliver the data to one side and bargain, or broadcast to everyone and lose all protection. Old betrayals surface; each accuses the other of repeating history. Emotional beat: the relationship's first true fracture.

chapters.title: The Second Signal
chapters.summary: Mara discovers the beacon was commissioned by the original Ashkari delegation—as a promise that someone would always listen. Her exile assignment was never random; she was chosen by the dead. Emotional beat: revelation reframing nine years of emptiness as vocation.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Climax begins. With both fleets in orbit and Okafor demanding compliance, Mara overrides the beacon and transmits the complete record on every channel, in every language she knows. The station burns power it can't spare. Emotional beat: terrible clarity; the point of no return.

chapters.title: Vesper-9 Falls Silent
chapters.summary: Okafor fires on the beacon array; the station goes dark with Mara inside. Ilex, presumed gone, turns the crippled scout ship between the guns and the transmitter and refuses to move. Emotional beat: sacrifice answered by sacrifice; the found family made literal.

chapters.title: Ceasefire in a Dead Language
chapters.summary: Both fleets receive the record simultaneously; neither can claim exclusive truth. Ashkari voices flood open channels, and soldiers on both sides begin answering in kind. Okafor stands down rather than fire on a rescue. Emotional beat: the war cracking along the seam of shared hearing.

chapters.title: Extraction
chapters.summary: Rescue teams pull Mara from the darkened station; she wakes to Ilex's voice counting in Ashkari. The survivors transmit coordinates and request the two of them personally as witnesses. Emotional beat: exhaustion, relief, the disbelief of having survived a choice.

chapters.title: Someone Will Always Listen
chapters.summary: Epilogue, alternating POVs. Months later, a new beacon rises over the Ashkari settlement, staffed voluntarily. Mara dreams again—this time in a language with living speakers. Emotional beat: belonging achieved not as refuge but as chosen, ongoing attention.
